sequence.title: Write-path utilities (apply_label is the missing one)
dod: apply_label creates a label at an arbitrary address, including one with no defined data -- that is the case the current path cannot handle
Java: a dedicated endpoint calling SymbolTable.createLabel(), NOT the getDefinedDataAt() branch inside renameDataAtAddress()
The endpoint reports success or failure; /renameData answers 'Rename data attempted' regardless, which is how this went unnoticed
Bridge tool with dry_run default and the GHIDRA_MCP_ENABLE_WRITES gate
Name collisions handled (see the script's make_unique_name)
rename_function and set_comment already exist and are unaffected
notes: Blocked in practice, not merely unimplemented: labelling MMIO registers at 0xB1006xxx was needed and could not be done through the plugin.

Root cause (verified 2026-08-20): the plugin's only createLabel() call is a fallback inside renameDataAtAddress(), guarded by listing.getDefinedDataAt(addr) != null. An unmapped MMIO register has no defined data, so the whole block is skipped. The /renameData handler ignores the outcome and always answers 'Rename data attempted'. The bridge exposes neither the endpoint nor any label tool.
Working around it: scripts/ghidra/import_mmio_labels.py, a Ghidra script that calls createLabel() unconditionally. It is what unblocked the work and shows what the endpoint has to do.
Needs a plugin rebuild, so it is a session of its own.

sequence.title: Undefined regions are reported, not skipped in silence
dod: disassemble_at carries coverage{requested_address,start_address,skipped_bytes,gaps[]} and a method_note whenever the listing does not start at the requested address or has holes
A listing that starts where it was asked and runs without holes carries neither key
disassemble_batch reports the same per address, computed before the query filter so a filtered listing is not mistaken for a gap
read_words reports unreadable_words and a method_note; read_bytes reports a method_note on a short read -- null is not zero
Schemas, OpenAPI snapshot and docs/api.md updated; tool descriptions stay under the schema-base ceiling
Unit coverage on the addresses the defect was found on (0x002818b0 -> 0x00286d94, 21732 bytes; pool 0x25b878-0x25b89b, 36 bytes)
notes: Root cause: handleDisassembleAt uses Listing.getInstructions(addr, true), a forward iterator over defined instructions, which starts at the next defined one without a marker.
Fixed bridge-side: the plugin already returns the real addresses, so the skip is computed from the response rather than requiring a plugin rebuild.
Verified live against the ZK-Inkjet program with the patched code.

sequence.title: size and range are defined and reconcile
dod: analyze_function_complete reports range.span_bytes = end - start + 1, documented as the bound including interior data
list_functions_in_range documents size as body bytes with interior data excluded, and that a thunk carries its target's name
Both schemas cross-reference the other number so neither can be read as the other
notes: Verified on FUN_0025b338: size 1696, span_bytes 1732, difference 36 bytes -- exactly the constant pool at 0x25b878-0x25b89b that disassemble_at now reports as a gap.
The hypothesis in the original entry was half right: size sums the body ranges, but the pool is interior rather than trailing.
The boot_init duplicate is not a second chunk: 0x273ee4 is a 4-byte thunk (b 0x0025b0c4) and Ghidra names thunks after their target. Exposing that needs the plugin -- see FUNC-CHUNKS-THUNKS.

sequence.title: Expose thunks and non-contiguous bodies in functionsInRange
dod: /functionsInRange emits span, thunk target and chunks behind fields=extended, so an older bridge keeps the format it parses
Bridge requests the fields and tolerates their absence; the payload is unchanged against a plugin that does not send them
list_functions_in_range surfaces is_thunk/thunk_to/span_bytes/chunks only where they say something
Decision recorded: size keeps its name, span_bytes is the unambiguous one -- renaming would be breaking
notes: Runtime-verified against the ZK-Inkjet program after the rebuild: boot_init at 0x00273ee4 reports thunk=0025b0c4, and FUN_0025b338 reports chunks 0025b338-0025b877 and 0025b89c-0025b9fb.

The numbers close: the chunks sum to 1696, which is size; the span is 1732; the 36-byte difference is the constant pool at 0x25b878-0x25b89b, which disassemble_at reports as a gap at the same addresses over a separate code path.
Backward compatibility verified in both directions: the old plugin ignored fields=extended, and the new plugin answers a request without it in the old format byte for byte.
